correctness.rationale: The positive quadratic P permits a global conserved Hamiltonian H=y^2/2+V(x), Vprime=x^3/P. V has two monotone branches, grows quadratically and yields a unique regular energy oval for each E>0. Original-time change of variables gives f_E=1_(V<E)/(J P sqrt(1-V/E)), T=sqrt(2/E)J, W(v)=x_+(v)^(-3)+|x_-(v)|^(-3). Its tail is c v^(-3/2)+O(v^-2), c=1/(sqrt(2) alpha^(3/2)); the Abel transform of the leading tail from v=1 is exactly 2c sqrt(1-1/E), cancelling the otherwise misleading E^(-1/2) normalization error. Remainder yields J-C=O(log E/E), C=2pi/sqrt(Delta). Outside-turning-point Cauchy tail Q/C=2c/(C sqrt(E))+O(E^-1); upper/lower L1 comparison gives the sharp TV coefficient, not just weak convergence. Independently computed turning-point tail for alpha=gamma=1 at E=100,1000,10000: scaled masses .3909077177,.3899998483,.3898651104 converge to predicted .3898484006. Infinite assertions rely on explicit analytic bounds, not the three values.
